decision_questions: Does the single completed final lexically retain the GT A-question tail (do/that) and C-head (You/have/to/hope)?
For each of the four offline boundary choices, which fragment holds each anchor word, and does the projected ownership agree with the known GT side at S?
Does any boundary choice separate the A/C phrases without dropping, duplicating, or splitting a character (exact conservation)?
What are the raw token timestamp ranges per group, and which groups straddle a boundary (ambiguous) or lack timestamps (unresolved)?
grouping_rule: English whitespace-delimited lexical groups over the finalized accepted stream, retaining exact original whitespace, punctuation, and subword content. Group scan: leading whitespace (if any) attaches to the first word; each subsequent group runs from the end of the previous word through the next word plus its trailing whitespace run, so concatenating groups in order reproduces the final text exactly. Whole-word RIGHT-END assignment: a group with estimated end_sample <= boundary goes left, else right; multiple boundaries apply in ascending order (fragment index = count of boundaries strictly below the group end). A group whose estimated interval strictly contains a boundary is flagged ambiguous but never split and never discarded. A group with missing end timestamp stays unresolved: no fictitious time fallback; its text is preserved in place and automatic ownership is reported unsupported. No text dedup by string: genuine repetitions are retained. No midpoint variant, no sweep.
